transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 16:00 UTC (08:00 PT)
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sarah (CISO Axion), Tom (Infra), Priya (DevOps), Ravi (Product)

Summary:
Quick intake on security posture for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Focus on SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS/encryption for PHI, data retention and network topology (VPC/private). Agreed to follow up with SOC2 artifacts and a technical deep dive.

Topics covered:
- Compliance posture: SOC 2 / ISO27001 status and timelines
- Identity: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC mapping
- Data controls: encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)
- Auditability: audit logs, retention, exportability, SIEM ingestion
- Deployment choices: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem), network egress, peering, firewall rules
- Retention and PHI handling (HIPAA considerations)

Action items (captured during call): see metadata/action_items above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey all thanks for joining, hey Sarah, Tom, Priya, Ravi, quick intros from our side — I'm Maya, AE, and Liam here is our SE who will take the deeper infra + KMS questions.
[00:12] Sarah (Axion CISO): Hi thanks, appreciate you fitting us in. We're early in vendor eval, main ask is can you lay out, uh, what controls Redwood has for PHI and how KMS and retention works.
[00:21] Liam (Redwood SE): Yep absolutely. High level we support hosted API, dedicated reserved clusters, and private deployments with a customer-controlled VPC. We can talk through key differences, like KMS — Redwood-managed keys vs customer-managed via BYOK/Cloud KMS.
[00:35] Tom (Axion Infra): Quick context: Axion is subject to HIPAA; we have a hybrid on-prem + cloud setup. Latency matters for some triage features but security requirements may push us towards private deployment. We're most worried about audit logs, SSO integration, and where keys live.
[00:50] Priya (DevOps): Also retention — we currently keep logs for 7 years for specific data classes, but for inference payloads we need clarity about retention, redaction, and deletion.
[01:05] Maya: Got it. I'll start with compliance artifacts: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO-27001 cert in process (or recent depending on date), we'll share the latest attestation. Our hosted product data retention defaults are X days but can be configured for enterprise — for PHI we'd recommend private or dedicated where you can control retention strictly.
[01:26] Ravi (Product): When you say 'control' for dedicated, do we get a separate tenant and isolation, or is it logical?
[01:34] Liam: Dedicated is tenant-isolated with reserved GPU pools — we provide strong data separation, separate project IDs, and access controls; private is a deployment that sits in your VPC or on-prem and you control the network and KMS. There's some differences in the management plane access which we can map out.
[01:52] Sarah: For auditors we need proof of SSH/logging, show me audit trails with user IDs and actions. How granular are Redwood's audit logs?
[02:02] Maya: We capture token-level usage, API calls, model versions used, and per-request metadata. Liam, want to detail exports?
[02:10] Liam: Sure — logs include caller identity, timestamp, request id, model variant, input size, response size, and error codes. We can stream audit logs to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Stackdriver) or push via syslog depending on the deployment. For private deployments you get direct integration into your log collectors.
[02:30] Tom: Can logs be redacted or filtered? We can't ship raw PHI into vendor-managed storage.
[02:37] Liam: Good question. For hosted, we redact sensitive fields at ingestion if you provide a filter set or use a preprocessor. For dedicated/private, you keep logs in your own environment so PHI doesn't leave your control. We also support tokenization and prefix-caching options so full content isn't persisted.
[02:57] Sarah: Encryption specifics — we need at-rest/ in-transit TLS and customer-managed KMS for at-rest. Is HSM supported?
[03:05] Maya: Yes TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit. For at-rest, hosted uses Redwood-managed encryption keys by default, with an enterprise option for customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault. HSM-backed keys via your cloud provider are supported; if you're on private we can integrate with your on-prem HSM via KMIP or cloud gateway depending on network.
[03:30] Priya: How about key rotation? Is there an automated rotation or manual?
[03:36] Liam: Rotation is handled by the KMS provider if you use CMK. We support rekeying and vault rotation policies — and we store minimal key metadata in the control plane and never the raw key material. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate on a schedule and provide attestations.
[03:52] Ravi: SSO — we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. How deep is your RBAC integration?
[04:00] Maya: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and built-in RBAC that maps to SCIM groups. You can create roles like admin, dev, readonly and map to groups in Okta. Liam, any caveats?
[04:12] Liam: Caveat: hosted is multi-tenant so roles map at org and project levels; in dedicated/private you can enforce stricter network-level controls and limit management plane access. Also note session durations and SAML assertion lifetimes — we can adjust per customer.
[04:32] Tom: Audit export format — is it JSON lines? CSV? We want native JSON to ingest to Splunk.
[04:39] Liam: We can stream as JSONL to S3 or push events to a webhook; Splunk forwarder can then ingest. For hosted we retain a rolling window unless you have retention add-on.
[04:58] Sarah: Does Redwood support artifact-level attestations like file integrity or WORM? We have compliance needs to show immutable logs.
[05:06] Maya: We do support immutable append-only logs in the private deployment and can provide write-once buckets for audit retention. For hosted, there are enterprise options to enable tamper-evident logs — we can share the tech note.
[05:25] Priya: Regarding PHI flows — if we use hosted with redaction enabled, how do you guarantee no copy remains in cache or transient storage?
[05:33] Liam: We have KV cache options; by default KV cache does not persist input data beyond the necessary lifetime, and cache entries can be encrypted. For PHI we advise disabling prefix/KV caching or use private deployment so caches live in your environment. There's also a config to purge caches on-demand.
[05:53] Tom: Network: can Redwood peer into our VPC? We need to avoid public egress for PHI.
[05:59] Maya: For private deployment we don't egress through public internet; you run inference inside your VPC. For dedicated and hosted we offer VPC peering or private interconnect options depending on region and cloud. We'll share network diagrams.
[06:17] Sarah: Ok this is helpful. On the legal chain — do you support BAA for HIPAA-covered entities?
[06:24] Maya: We do offer a BAA for enterprise customers, yes. It's tied to deployment mode — typically dedicated/private is required for BAAs but we can discuss exceptions. We'll send templated language.
[06:35] Ravi: Competitor note — we talked to a few folks who push for simpler hosted integration (OpenAI) but security teams didn't like opaque retention. Do you get many customers migrating from hosted to private?
[06:47] Liam: Yes, that's common as workloads mature — teams start hosted for speed then move to dedicated/private for compliance or cost predictability. We provide migration guides.
[06:58] Priya: Any SOC2 gaps we should know about today?
[07:03] Maya: Nothing major — we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report. There are always some environment-specific controls auditors ask for; we'll work with your security team to map.
[07:12] Sarah: Can you show mapping to our control sets, for example how your logging maps to our control IDs?
[07:19] Liam: Yes we can produce a control-mapping matrix once we see your checklist; that will be part of the technical deep dive.
[07:27] Maya: Quick practical Qs — Priya, what's your typical SLA requirement for latency and uptime?
[07:32] Priya: 99.9% uptime and p95 latency under 300ms for the triage flows; other batch processes can be higher. If private gives us lower jitter that's preferable.
[07:44] Liam: Dedicated can meet those p95 numbers with reserved GPU throughput; private on-prem might be even lower latency but depends on your hardware. We do continuous batching and KV cache but if you disable caching for PHI, cost goes up and latency might be slightly higher.
[08:05] Tom: Curious about cost tradeoffs, but we mainly wanted to validate security before budgeting.
[08:12] Maya: Understood. We'll send a pricing snapshot for hosted vs dedicated vs private after the compliance docs.
[08:18] Sarah: Regarding data deletion — if a user requests deletion, what's the process end-to-end?
[08:24] Liam: For hosted: we have data deletion APIs and processes; we purge stored inputs and associated artifacts within the agreed RTO, and we can provide deletion certificates for audit. For private/dedicated, deletion is in your control and we can provide a recommended process and scripts.
[08:44] Priya: The deletion certificate — is that fully automated? We need the ability to run periodic compliance checks.
[08:50] Maya: We have automation to confirm deletion on request and logs showing deletion events; we'll share the template for the certificate.
[08:58] Ravi: A slightly awkward question: how do you handle model updates and potential model-regression alerts — we need guardrails for hallucinations in PHI contexts.
[09:07] Liam: Good point. We support pinned model versions per-deployment and rollouts with canary policies. For PHI-critical flows you'd pin to vetted model and enable deterministic filters; we also have quality monitoring and eval hooks to trigger rollbacks if regressions occur.
[09:28] Sarah: Does Redwood do red-team or adversarial testing for PHI leak scenarios?
[09:34] Maya: We have internal eval suites and can coordinate custom adversarial tests as an engagement. That would be part of a deeper security assessment.
[09:45] Tom: Ok, can we schedule the technical deep dive next week — Liam, you'll run it?
[09:51] Liam: Yes, we can do a 45-minute SE deep dive for private deployment and KMS integration. How's 2026-02-24 10:00 PT?
[09:59] Priya: Works for me.
[10:02] Sarah: Works for me too.
[10:04] Maya: Great. As for docs, I'll send: SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, network diagram, BAA template, and our KMS integration note. Liam will send runbook and sample audit export configuration.
[10:17] Ravi: Anything else — third-party subprocessors? We need list for vendor checks.
[10:22] Maya: We'll include subprocessors list in the compliance pack.
[10:25] Priya: One more — can we get a test tenant with no data so we can run connectivity tests?
[10:30] Liam: We can provision a sandbox org on hosted or a staging dedicated cluster for networking tests. We'll coordinate in the next steps.
[10:40] Sarah: Cool. For the follow up, please include a short matrix mapping your features to our top control IDs, that will speed the audit.
[10:48] Maya: We'll do that.
[10:52] Closing recap by Maya: We'll send artifacts (SOC2, ISO summary, BAA template, network diagram), Liam schedules technical deep dive on 2026-02-24 10:00 PT, Priya to share retention and PHI flow doc, and we'll reconvene after the SE call to confirm path (likely dedicated or private).
[11:10] Sarah: Thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[11:14] Tom: Thanks.
[11:16] Maya: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Recorded notes: Some speaker labels may be approximate; a few words were garbled in transcription (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of KV cache) — please rely on the action items for concrete follow-ups.
